finding.claim: Cached verification results ignore the token's exp claim when the payload has no numeric iat. The cache entry then lives for the full cacheTTL (default 600s) and expired tokens keep verifying successfully. An attacker holding a validly signed token that has exp but no iat can keep using it for up to cacheTTL after it expires. This happens whenever caching is enabled and the issuer omits iat (for example, signer option noTimestamp).
finding.source: A validly signed JWT with an `exp` claim and no numeric `iat`, replayed to a verifier created with `cache` enabled. The attacker only needs to present it before expiry and again after expiry, within cacheTTL.
finding.sink: verify() cache-hit branch at src/verifier.js:363-378 returns the cached payload via handleCachedResult without re-running exp validation.

trace.note: A successful verification calls cacheSet(cacheContext, payload).
hasIat is false when payload.iat is not a number.
The block that sets cacheValue[1] (nbf) and cacheValue[2] (exp / maxAge) is gated on hasIat and is skipped, so cacheValue[2] stays 0.
cacheValue[2] is 0, so it becomes maxTTL. Expiry is never capped to payload.exp.
On a later call, (max === 0 || now <= max) passes even though now > exp.
The cached payload is returned without re-running the exp validator.

finding.guards_checked: The exp validator in verifyToken (src/verifier.js:304-323) runs only on a cache miss. The cache-hit time-range check uses only cached min/max, which were not derived from exp here. The cacheTTL upper bound limits the window but does not remove it. errorCacheTTL applies only to errors. No other layer rechecks exp on a cache hit.
